title: AML enforcement: six cases, practical control tests
seoTitle: AML enforcement: six cases and practical control tests
excerpt: Six selected records from July 2025 to July 2026 suggest tests for monitoring, customer due diligence and independent AML testing. This dated sample is not a measure of global enforcement trends.
content:
## A focused six-record sample

This brief draws on six selected source records dated from 30 July 2025 to 28 July 2026: four FINRA matters, one Austrian Financial Market Authority (FMA) matter and one AUSTRAC proceeding. The examples concern different business activities and procedural stages. They support practical control questions, not a claim about the direction or prevalence of global AML enforcement.

FINRA records describe deficiencies in monitoring activity tied to the firm's business, in ongoing customer due diligence, and in independent AML testing. Outset Global Trading Limited's outsourced trading desk handled equities and options for institutional customers, including thinly traded low-priced securities. FINRA said the AML programme was not reasonably designed to detect and report suspicious transactions in that business; the firm was censured and fined $130,000. [Read FINRA's action concerning Outset Global Trading](https://www.finra.org/sites/default/files/fda_documents/2024080217601%20Outset%20Global%20Trading%20Limited%20CRD%20281065%20AWC%20vrp.pdf).

FINRA also censured and fined RBC Capital Markets, LLC $275,000 for failing to develop and implement an AML compliance programme reasonably designed to detect and cause the reporting of suspicious transactions. The described period ran from February 2016 through September 2023. [Read FINRA's action concerning RBC Capital Markets](https://www.finra.org/sites/default/files/fda_documents/2022075967301%20RBC%20Capital%20Markets%20LLC%20CRD%2031194%20AWC%20lp%20.pdf).

Beta Capital Securities LLC, doing business as Creand Securities, was censured and fined $145,000. FINRA described both an AML programme not reasonably designed to detect suspicious transactions and inadequate risk-based procedures for ongoing customer due diligence between October 2019 and July 2023. [Read FINRA's action concerning Beta Capital](https://www.finra.org/sites/default/files/fda_documents/2022073419001%20Beta%20Capital%20Securities%20LLC%20dba%20Creand%20Securities%20CRD%2038964%20AWC%20lp.pdf).

A separate FINRA action against MCAP LLC concerned testing rather than transaction monitoring: the firm conducted no independent AML testing in 2021 and 2022, and testing in 2023 and 2024 was unreasonable. FINRA censured the firm and imposed a $15,000 fine. [Read FINRA's action concerning MCAP](https://www.finra.org/sites/default/files/fda_documents/2023077010801%20MCAP%20LLC%20CRD%20139515%20AWC%20ks.pdf).

Austria's Financial Market Authority fined Sparkasse Oberösterreich Bank AG €60,000. Its final penal order concerned policies and procedures for understanding customer ownership and control structures, applying that understanding on an ongoing basis, and updating required information, data and documents. [Read the Austrian FMA notice concerning Sparkasse Oberösterreich](https://www.fma.gv.at/en/announcement-fma-imposes-sanction-upon-sparkasse-oberosterreich-bank-ag-for-breach-of-due-diligence-obligations-for-the-prevention-of-money-laundering-and-terrorist-financing/).

AUSTRAC's record is different in status. On 30 July 2025, it applied for civil penalty orders against Mount Pritchard and District Community Club Ltd, alleging serious and systemic non-compliance with Australia's AML/CTF laws. The announcement describes an application based on allegations, not a final penalty determination; this brief does not assess subsequent court developments. [Read AUSTRAC's announcement concerning Mount Pritchard](https://www.austrac.gov.au/news-and-media/media-release/austrac-launches-civil-penalty-proceedings-against-pokies-giant-mounties).

## Turn the examples into evidence requests

The Outset and RBC matters suggest a useful monitoring test: can the firm show that scenarios and thresholds reflect its actual products, counterparties, customers and transaction patterns? Evidence could include a documented risk-to-scenario map, alert samples, investigation files, exception decisions and outcomes from scenario tuning. The test is not simply whether a monitoring system exists, but whether its design and operation can be demonstrated for the business being supervised.

The Beta and Sparkasse matters make customer due diligence a traceability question. For a sample of higher-risk relationships, can staff connect identity and ownership evidence to the customer-risk decision, refresh schedule, transaction activity and any escalation? A reviewer should be able to see what information was missing, who accepted an exception, why it was accepted, and when it must be revisited.

The MCAP matter suggests that independent testing needs evidence of independence and follow-through. Request the approved testing plan, scope rationale, tester reporting line, workpapers, findings log, accountable owners, target dates and retest results. If a test was delayed or narrowed, the reason and residual risk should be visible to management.

The AUSTRAC proceeding adds a case-status control: internal dashboards, board papers and customer-facing summaries should label an application or allegation as such until an authoritative outcome changes its status. A procedural status field should be maintained separately from the underlying allegation and any later order.

## Practical questions for management and boards

1. Which products, customer types and counterparties are covered by each AML monitoring scenario, and what evidence supports the calibration?
2. Can a reviewer trace customer ownership and risk information from onboarding through refresh and transaction review?
3. Who approves exceptions when required evidence is incomplete, and how are those exceptions time-limited and monitored?
4. Is independent testing risk-based, sufficiently independent, and followed by documented remediation and retesting?
5. Do reports preserve whether a matter is alleged, settled, final or still before a court or regulator?

These are analytical review prompts, not legal advice or regulator-mandated wording.

## Key Takeaways

* Ask for a risk-to-monitoring map, representative alert files and evidence that scenario tuning reflects the firm's real activity.
* Sample customer files end to end: ownership evidence, risk decision, refresh history, transaction review and escalation.
* Review exception logs for accountable approval, rationale, expiry date and follow-up evidence.
* Require independent-testing plans, workpapers, findings owners, remediation dates and retest results.
* Label applications and allegations separately from settled or final outcomes in dashboards and board materials.

## About the Data

The article uses six unique source records from three regulators: FINRA, Austria's FMA and AUSTRAC. The records span 30 July 2025 to 28 July 2026. Five records contain verified monetary amounts, representing five distinct currency-and-amount pairs; the AUSTRAC record concerns an application for civil penalty orders and has no verified penalty amount. The selected records are not a complete catalogue and cannot establish a global enforcement trend.
